Name: fold_specific_learning_rates
Title: Fold Layer-specific Learning Rates: Optimizing Training Dynamics in PPO with Soft Fold Layers
Experiment: Implement fold layer-specific learning rates, where the fold layers have a different learning rate than the linear layers. Compare the training dynamics, convergence speed, and final performance with the baseline model.

Name: input_dependent_hyperplane_combination
Title: Input-Dependent Hyperplane Combination in Soft Fold Layers: Enhancing Adaptability in PPO
Experiment: Modify the SoftFold layer to learn a set of basis normal vectors and combine them based on input-dependent weights. Replace the single normal vector 'n' with a learnable matrix 'N' of shape (num_basis, width), where num_basis is a hyperparameter. Add a small neural network (e.g., a single linear layer followed by a softmax activation) that takes the input tensor as input and outputs a weight vector of shape (num_basis,). The forward pass will compute the weighted sum of the basis normal vectors using these weights: n = sum(weights[i] * N[i]) for i in range(num_basis). Normalize the resulting vector 'n' to ensure it has unit length. The forward pass will then use this dynamically combined 'n' to compute the folding effect. Experiment with different values for num_basis (e.g., 2, 4, 8) and different architectures for the weight prediction network (e.g., adding a hidden layer, using different activation functions). Compare the training dynamics, convergence speed, and final performance with the baseline model using a fixed 'n'.

Name: pheromone_inspired_directional_noise
Title: Pheromone-Inspired Directional Noise Injection in Soft Fold Layers: Enhancing Exploration in PPO
Experiment: Modify the SoftFold layer to inject noise into the direction of the normal vector 'n' before each forward pass. Add a new parameter 'noise_scale' to the SoftFold class, which represents the scale of the noise. This parameter can be either a learnable parameter or a fixed hyperparameter. If noise_scale is input-dependent, add a small neural network (e.g., a single linear layer followed by a Sigmoid activation) that takes the input tensor as input and outputs the noise_scale. In the forward pass, sample a random direction vector 'd' from a Gaussian distribution with mean 0 and standard deviation 1, and normalize it to unit length. Then, add 'noise_scale' * 'd' to the normalized 'n'. Re-normalize 'n' after adding the noise. Compare the training dynamics, convergence speed, and final performance of the PPO agent with the modified SoftFold layer to the baseline model on the LunarLander-v3 environment. Track the episodic return, gradient norms, and parameter norms to evaluate the impact of the noise injection. Experiment with different values for the fixed 'noise_scale' (e.g., 0.01, 0.05, 0.1) and different architectures for the noise_scale prediction network (e.g., adding a hidden layer) if an input-dependent noise_scale is used.

They are interested in the behavioral and physiological effects of pheromones, as well as their potential applications in fields such as agriculture, animal behavior, and forensic science.

Name: gated_residual_softfold_layer
Title: Gated Residual Soft Fold Layer: Adaptive Feature Transformation with a Single Folding Operation
Experiment: Modify the Agent class to replace each existing SoftFold layer with a single gated residual SoftFold layer. The gated residual SoftFold layer consists of a SoftFold layer, a learnable gate (a sigmoid activated linear layer that takes the output of the SoftFold layer as input and outputs a scalar between 0 and 1), and a residual connection. Multiply the output of the SoftFold layer by the gate value. Add a residual connection from the input of the SoftFold layer to the output of the gated SoftFold layer. Compare the training dynamics, convergence speed, and final performance with the baseline model using a single SoftFold layer. Track the episodic return, gradient norms, and parameter norms to evaluate the impact of the gated residual SoftFold layer.

Name: learnable_input_scaling_shifting
Title: Learnable Input Scaling and Shifting for Soft Fold Layers: Improving Feature Representation in PPO
Experiment: Modify the Agent class to add learnable scaling and shifting parameters before the first SoftFold layer in both the actor and critic networks. Replace the nn.Linear layer with two nn.Parameter tensors: scale and shift, both with the same shape as the input observation space. The forward pass would then simply be: scaled_input = input * scale + shift. Compare the training dynamics, convergence speed, and final performance with the baseline model. Track the episodic return, gradient norms, parameter norms, and the learned scaling and shifting parameters to evaluate the impact of input pre-processing.

Name: input_dependent_hyperplane_magnitude
Title: Input-Dependent Hyperplane Magnitude in Soft Fold Layers: Enhancing Responsiveness in PPO
Experiment: Modify the SoftFold layer to make the hyperplane magnitude input-dependent. Add a small neural network (e.g., a single linear layer followed by a sigmoid activation to ensure positive magnitude) that takes the input tensor as input and outputs a scalar representing the shift magnitude. In the forward pass, compute the shift magnitude based on the input. Then, scale the normal vector 'n' by this magnitude: n_scaled = n * shift_magnitude. Normalize the n_scaled vector. Use the scaled and normalized normal vector n_scaled in the subsequent calculations (x_dot_n, n_dot_n, etc.). Experiment with different architectures for the shift magnitude prediction network (e.g., adding a hidden layer). Compare the training dynamics, convergence speed, and final performance with the baseline model using a fixed hyperplane position. Track the episodic return, gradient norms, and parameter norms to evaluate the impact of the input-dependent hyperplane magnitude.

Name: context_modulated_softfold
Title: Context-Modulated Soft Fold Layer: Adaptive Hyperplane Behavior through Global State Representation in PPO
Experiment: Modify the SoftFold layer to remove the learnable crease and stretch parameters. Add a context network (a small MLP with 2 layers of 32 units each) that takes the input observation as input and outputs predictions for the crease and stretch parameters. Use sigmoid activation for the stretch prediction to ensure positivity, and linear activation for the crease (or a Tanh to keep it bounded). These predictions are then used as the crease and stretch parameters in the forward pass of the SoftFold layer. Compare the training dynamics, convergence speed, and final performance with the baseline model. Analyze the learned context vectors and the predicted crease and stretch values to understand how the network is adapting the SoftFold layer's behavior. Add L1 regularization to the weights of the context network to encourage feature selection.

Name: input_dependent_normal_vector_scaling
Title: Input-Dependent Normal Vector Scaling in Soft Fold Layers: Feature-Specific Hyperplane Adaptation in PPO
Experiment: Modify the SoftFold layer to implement input-dependent scaling of the normal vector 'n'. Add a small neural network (e.g., a single linear layer followed by a ReLU activation) that takes the input tensor as input and outputs a vector of the same shape as 'n'. In the forward pass, multiply the normal vector 'n' element-wise by the scaling factors predicted by the network. Normalize the resulting vector to maintain a consistent magnitude. Use the scaled and normalized normal vector in the subsequent calculations (x_dot_n, n_dot_n, etc.). Compare the training dynamics, convergence speed, and final performance with the baseline model. Track the episodic return, gradient norms, and parameter norms to evaluate the impact of the feature-specific scaling.

Name: feature_wise_input_scaling_softfold
Title: Feature-Wise Input Scaling with Learnable Magnitude in Soft Fold Layers: Adaptive Feature Transformation in PPO
Experiment: Modify the SoftFold layer to implement feature-wise input scaling of the residual vector with a learnable magnitude. Add a learnable scalar parameter 'input_scale' to the SoftFold layer. In the forward pass, compute the residual vector (the difference between the input and its orthogonal projection onto the hyperplane). Multiply the residual vector element-wise by the input tensor, and then multiply the result by the learnable scalar 'input_scale'. Add the scaled residual vector to the input tensor. Compare the training dynamics, convergence speed, and final performance with the baseline model. Track the episodic return, gradient norms, and parameter norms to evaluate the impact of the feature-wise input scaling.

Name: direction_aware_crease
Title: Direction-Aware Crease in Soft Fold Layers: Enhancing Geometric Adaptability in PPO
Experiment: Modify the SoftFold layer to incorporate a direction-aware crease. Instead of a separate network, directly use the dot product of the input and the normal vector (x_dot_n) to modulate the crease parameter. In the forward pass, compute x_dot_n (input_tensor @ self.n). Apply a sigmoid function to x_dot_n: sigmoid(x_dot_n). Multiply the original crease parameter by this sigmoid value to obtain the direction-aware crease: direction_aware_crease = self.crease * sigmoid(x_dot_n). Use the direction-aware crease in the subsequent calculations in the forward pass, replacing the original self.crease. Compare the training dynamics, convergence speed, and final performance with the baseline model. Track the episodic return, gradient norms, and parameter norms to evaluate the impact of the direction-aware crease.
